title: Edmund and the Thorn
premise: Oscar Marchetti, a runaway hedge-witch's apprentice living under a false name in a city that outlawed magic, discovers that the fallen border wards were bound to a living thorn-tree tended by Edmund Hale, the boy he abandoned fifteen years ago. The wards didn't fail — they were fed to something ancient by the city's founders, who traded the kingdom's memory-magic for their own survival during the last war. As the stars go out and forgotten things crawl back over the border, Oscar must return to the village he fled, reconcile with the dying Edmund who kept his secret all these years, and choose whether to pour his own memories into the thorn to rekindle the wards. He does — but Edmund secretly splits the price with him, and both survive half-remembered, together.
about_author: Quentin Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from rural herbalists and village healers before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about small magics, broken promises, and the people who stay behind.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the city of Vell, Oscar sells luck-knots and fever-charms disguised as folk trinkets, hiding his training since fleeing apprenticeship fifteen years ago. A child customer's charm actually works, drawing the attention of a Warden of the Unmaking. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a gift buried alive.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The border wards collapse with a sound like a struck bell; every star above Vell gutters dark at once. Panic floods the streets while Oscar feels the old magic wake in his bones. Emotional beat: terror and a shameful flicker of homecoming.

chapters.title: The Warden's Question
chapters.summary: Warden Isolde Crane's POV. Crane interrogates charm-sellers, hunting whoever's magic resonated with the falling wards. She spares Oscar on a whim — or so it seems — marking him instead. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse dread; Crane is revealed as dutiful, not cruel.

chapters.title: A Letter Written in Sap
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A courier delivers a letter sealed with thorn-sap: Edmund is dying, the tree is failing, come home. The handwriting is the boy's, grown older. Oscar burns it, then digs the ashes out of the grate. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a scar torn open.

chapters.title: What the Hedge Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Fleeing Vell ahead of Crane, Oscar travels the old hedgeroads, where memory-magic lingers in blackberry and elder. The hedges show him fragments of his apprenticeship under Mother Aldith. Emotional beat: grief braided with tenderness for the life he discarded.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. His home village has lost its own name; no one remembers the war, the tree, or him. Only Edmund's house still holds its memories, guarded by a door that knows Oscar's true name. Emotional beat: the horror of inheritance squandered.

chapters.title: Edmund, Keeper of the Thorn
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund, coughing blood, tends the great thorn-tree whose roots are the border wards. He has fed it his own memories for years to keep it alive. Seeing Oscar, he laughs and weeps at once. Emotional beat: reunion as reckoning — no anger, only terrible relief.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Winter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund recounts how Mother Aldith died holding the wards, how he took up the burden alone, and how he never told anyone Oscar's name when the Wardens came asking. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered before it is asked for.

chapters.title: The Founders' Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with Edmund. In Aldith's hidden cellar they find her journals: the city's founders survived the last war by feeding the kingdom's stored memories to the thing beyond the border, buying peace and calling it victory. Emotional beat: righteous fury at an inherited lie.

chapters.title: Crane Follows the Hedgeroad
chapters.summary: Isolde Crane's POV. Crane tracks Oscar, uncovering the same journals' copies in Vell's sealed archive. Her faith in the Unmaking wavers as she realizes the Wardens were built to guard the lie. Emotional beat: a believer's world quietly cracking.

chapters.title: Things That Crawl Back
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Starless night brings the first forgotten things across the border: creatures made of other people's discarded memories. The village fights them with pitchforks and prayer. Emotional beat: ordinary courage against the unrememberable.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund tells Oscar what rekindling the wards requires: a living mind poured into the thorn, memories and self alike. He intends to finish the job tonight, before he dies anyway. Emotional beat: calm acceptance that reads, to Oscar, like abandonment.

chapters.title: An Argument at the Root
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar and Edmund fight bitterly — fifteen years of flight versus fifteen years of duty. Oscar refuses to let Edmund die alone again; Edmund refuses to let Oscar pay for a choice he already made once. Emotional beat: love expressed as stubbornness.

chapters.title: Mother Aldith's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Among the journals, Oscar finds Aldith's final page: the ward need not take everything — shared willingly between two keepers, the cost divides. But no one has ever tried. Emotional beat: hope arriving too late to be comfortable.

chapters.title: Crane at the Door
chapters.summary: Isolde Crane's POV. Crane arrives to arrest Oscar and finds the village besieged. She spends her Warden authority defending it instead, then stands before the thorn and asks what she can do. Emotional beat: defection not as betrayal but as conscience.

chapters.title: The Stars Return, Wrongly
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A false dawn: stars relight, but arranged in patterns no one remembers, and the things at the border go quiet — waiting. The founders' bargain is being renegotiated by something on the other side. Emotional beat: dread dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What the Thorn Shows Oscar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Touching the tree, Oscar experiences the memories it holds — including Edmund's fifteen years of solitary nights, and one memory of himself running away, kept tenderly. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rite of Two Keepers
chapters.summary: Oscar and Edmund's alternating POV. At moonset they begin the rite together, Crane anchoring them with Warden craft turned inside out. The thorn drinks deep; the border flares green-gold. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar wakes missing huge swaths of himself — his mother's face, his years in Vell — but Edmund, who gave more, remembers even less. They hold hands and trade each other's pasts back piece by piece. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt from absence.

chapters.title: The Thing Beyond the Border
chapters.summary: Climax. The ancient hungry thing, cheated of a full meal, presses the border itself. The two keepers, the thorn, and Crane hold the line through one endless night, feeding it not memories but names — renaming it smaller and smaller until it fits behind the wards. Emotional beat: triumph won by wit and shared burden, not power.

chapters.title: A City Without Magic Learns Why
chapters.summary: Falling action. Crane returns to Vell with proof of the founders' bargain; the Wardens are remade as wardens of truth. Oscar, unable to go back to his old false life, stays — half a man, wholly present. Emotional beat: justice without spectacle.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Resolution, Edmund's POV. Spring comes to the village, which slowly remembers its name. Edmund and Oscar tend the tree together, planting a second thorn beside it — two roots, one wall. Emotional beat: quiet joy; survival was the price, and companionship is the change returned.
